extracted.intended_audience: EPA risk assessors and rulewriters; regulatory decisionmakers, lawyers, and environmental stakeholders
extracted.subtask_short: residual risk assessment review for oil and gas
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluation and recommended standards for EPA's residual risk and multipathway/cumulative risk assessment for oil and natural gas source categories under CAA §112(f)(2), with emphasis on child-protective methods, inclusion of all relevant HAPs and pathways, and cumulative impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full multipathway risk assessment including child scenarios
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA must perform a full multipathway risk assessment for the oil and gas sector that fully accounts for the greater multipathway exposure and risk for children, particularly in urban settings such as Los Angeles where drilling is occurring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The multipathway assessment should not be limited or dismissed as negligible; it must evaluate exposures from multiple media and pathways that could be significant for children and other vulnerable subpopulations. EPA must include exposed child scenarios as part of the cumulative risk assessment rather than ignoring them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess soil contamination exposures (direct and indirect hand-to-mouth/object-to-mouth)
rubrics_metrics.description: Risks from exposure to soil contaminants should evaluate both direct exposure, hand-to-mouth, and indirect, object-to-mouth, exposure, because soil contaminants are a particular risk to children due to play activities and behaviors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use updated estimates of incidental soil ingestion from the 2011 Exposure Factors Handbook and EPA's 2008 child-specific exposure factors. Recognize studies showing toddlers touch objects and put them in their mouths (e.g., average 15 times/hour, 90th percentile 66 times/hour) and correlations with blood lead levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use updated exposure factor guidance (2011 EFH and 2008 child-specific handbook)
rubrics_metrics.description: Past risk assessments have relied on outdated estimates of incidental soil ingestion exposures and EPA must update these values using the 2011 Exposure Factors Handbook and the 2008 Child-Specific Exposure Factors Handbook.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate recent studies and estimates of hand-to-mouth and object-to-mouth behavior in children into exposure calculations; explicitly address and use child-specific exposure factors in rulemaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not limit multipathway assessment to PB-HAPs; include other persistent/bioaccumulative HAPs
rubrics_metrics.description: The multipathway risk assessment was restricted only to contaminants identified as persistent and bioaccumulative (PB-HAPs), but the 2003 Guidance does not require such a restriction and EPA must evaluate other HAPs that present multipathway risk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include contaminants that persist and may bioaccumulate or biomagnify, even if not on the PB-HAP list; restricting to a predefined list underestimates risks from HAPs emitted by the source category and ignores soil contamination pathways.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate specific persistent/bioaccumulative HAPs (e.g., beryllium, arsenic, naphthalene, mercury)
rubrics_metrics.description: Chemicals such as beryllium and arsenic (expected to contaminate soils), naphthalene (PAH/POM), and mercury are persistent and bioaccumulative and were omitted or inadequately assessed; EPA must assess their multipathway risks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess inhalation, ingestion (soil and fish), and other relevant pathways for each chemical, both individually and cumulatively. Do not assume ingestion risks are zero for chemicals (e.g., arsenic) when evidence shows bioaccumulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess risk based on allowable emissions of all HAPs and potential concurrent emissions
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA fails to justify why circumstances allowing a facility to emit greater benzene would not also result in concurrent, additional emissions of other HAPs; allowable emissions must be considered for all HAPs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate potential for higher emissions, intermittent spikes, and accumulation over time; consider that small intermittent releases can accumulate in the environment and produce significant multipathway risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Add multipathway risk to inhalation risk to produce total risk
rubrics_metrics.description: The purpose of the multipathway assessment is to look at overall exposures — not just inhalation or other pathways in isolation — and EPA must add each type of risk to arrive at a total risk number for §112(f)(2) analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine multipathway-derived risks with inhalation risks before proceeding to determine acceptability and necessary standards and margins of safety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for increased exposure and vulnerability of children and pregnant women (including in utero exposures)
rubrics_metrics.description: The residual risk assessment underestimates risks by failing to account for increased susceptibility of children and the developing fetus to HAP exposure; early-life biological differences can increase cancer and non-cancer risks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate NAS recommendations, include in utero exposures as periods of increased sensitivity, and evaluate differential susceptibility for both cancer and non-cancer endpoints. Use best available science to assess early life vulnerability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply OEHHA age-dependent adjustment factors (ADAFs) for all carcinogens and include prenatal susceptibility
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA currently restricts application of the 2005 Supplemental Guidance to a limited set of mutagenic carcinogens; instead EPA must apply OEHHA ADAFs for all carcinogens and include prenatal susceptibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Update carcinogen lists and dose–response applications to reflect more recent evaluations and apply ADAFs broadly rather than limiting to pre-2006 lists or only mutagenic-mode carcinogens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use OEHHA child-specific reference doses for non-cancer impacts where available
rubrics_metrics.description: OEHHA has developed child-specific reference doses (ChRDs) for chronic noncancer and acute health risk and EPA should use them where they exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translate OEHHA ChRDs for oral, inhalation, and other pathway assessments to better account for children's greater exposure and vulnerability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply a Children's Default Safety Factor of ten for non-cancer endpoints when child-specific data are unavailable
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a child-specific reference value or vulnerability information is not available, EPA must apply at least a ten-fold margin of safety to protect children for chronic (non-cancer) and acute impacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a 10X default safety factor in addition to existing uncertainty factors to provide a conservative level of protection for infants and children under §112(f)(2), consistent with FQPA precedent and the CAA 'margin of safety' requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perform cumulative impacts analysis including background concentrations, multiple sources, pathways, and contaminants
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA's residual risk assessment underestimates risk by inadequately assessing cumulative risk from multiple sources, multiple HAPs, and multiple pathways; cumulative risk assessment must include aggregate exposures by multiple pathways, media and routes over time, plus combined exposures to multiple contaminants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow EPA resource documents, NAS, and SAB recommendations: include background and incremental risks, consider agents with similar modes of action, and present results in the broader context of aggregate and cumulative risks for decisionmakers and communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess combined exposures to other source categories and baseline contamination (maximum exposed individual context)
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA must assess total HAP emissions to which the maximum exposed individual is exposed, including baseline levels, sources outside the source category, and other nearby sources; refusal to do so underestimates total risk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider facility-wide risk, exposures from multiple facilities and source categories, and provide documentation of sources considered; do not rely on 'uncertainty' as a rationale for omission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct sensitivity analyses to identify, explain, and reduce major uncertainties
rubrics_metrics.description: The SAB recommended performing sensitivity analyses to identify major uncertainties in human health and ecological risk assessments, explain them clearly in the risk characterization, and take steps to reduce them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA should describe uncertainties, be conservative where public health is concerned, and take steps to reduce the largest sources of uncertainty rather than using them to justify omission of analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Update carcinogen listings and dose–response values to reflect recent evaluations and early-life susceptibility
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA's list of carcinogenic HAPs was generated in 2006 and must be updated to incorporate more recent evaluations of carcinogenic modes of action and early-life susceptibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revise dose–response values and pollutant lists to account for non-mutagenic carcinogen increased risk in early life and prenatal periods, per NAS and OEHHA findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjust dose–response and assessment approaches for specific HAPs showing increased early-life susceptibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The assessment must adjust for increased early-life susceptibility for particular HAPs emitted by the sector (examples cited: benzene, formaldehyde, POM/PAHs, arsenic, methylene chloride, acrolein).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each named HAP, evaluate the literature (e.g., CalEPA/OEHHA reviews, animal and human studies) and apply age-dependent adjustments or child-specific RfDs/uncertainty factors as appropriate (e.g., benzene prenatal/child susceptibility; OEHHA 10-fold factors for acrolein; PAH prenatal effects).
